newsitem.title: UK: Garantia cuts Petrobras earnings forecast.
newsitem.headline: Garantia cuts Petrobras earnings forecast.

text.p: Brazilian investment bank Garantia SA said on Thursday it has cut its earnings forecast for state-controlled oil conglomerate Petrobras but said it still rated its shares a short term buy.

"Although we are now working in a scenario where Petrobras spends 60 million reais per year more than we had previously been forecasting, we believe that the current stock price signals a buy opportunity in the short run," Garantia said in a statement released in London.

The investment bank said it had reduced its forecast for the company's 1996 net income to $804 million from $1,051 million. For 1997 it is forecasting net income of $751 million rather than the $814 it predicted previously.

The 1996 downwards revision is due both to some 139 million reais in extraordinary losses, representing provisions and settlement of various accounts owed to and receivable from the government, and to an increase of approximately 210 million reais in contributions to the company's pension fund.
Garantia analyst Oliver Mizne said a hydrocarbon law being discussed in Brazil's lower house would probably be voted on in December or January, with speedy progress likely through the senate.
"In this scenario, the new hydrocarbon law could be in place by the first half of 1997, reducing bureaucracy," he said, and making Petrobras' operations more flexible.
"In the long term, the changes taking place in the oil sector should be favourable to the company," he added.
He said Garantia maintained the company's "attractive" rating.
Petrobras preferred shares opened on Thursday at 120.50 reais. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
